recentItems.title: Brooklyn News Today: Teen slashed, 18-year-old shot, robbery suspects sought
recentItems.description:
Police are investigating a series of incidents across Brooklyn, including the slashing of a 15-year-old on Kings Highway, a Williamsburg shooting that left an 18-year-old in critical condition, gunfire reported near Foster Avenue, and a string of alleged gunpoint robberies and carjackings involving two teens. Authorities are also searching for suspects in separate robbery and theft cases, while Hakeem Smith is expected to be sentenced in the killing of Douglas Young. The roundup also includes a legal challenge involving school rankings and Success Academy charter schools.

recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Shootings, armed robberies and gun bust shake borough
recentItems.description:
The NYPD is investigating multiple incidents across the Bronx, including a shots-fired call on Creston Avenue, a case involving four women accused of firing a handgun on Briggs Avenue, and a slashing on East Tremont Avenue that left a 44-year-old man injured but expected to recover. Authorities are also searching for suspects in two armed robberies in Claremont and near Crotona Park, while three men were indicted in an alleged illegal gun trafficking conspiracy involving firearms purchased in Virginia for resale in New York. The roundup also includes the opening of the Bronx School of Hip-Hop’s new Webster Avenue campus and its first freshman class.

recentItems.title: Pilot loses engine power, makes incredible landing in Robert Moses beach parking lot
recentItems.description:

David Windmiller safely guided the aircraft into an empty parking lot at Field 4, avoiding vehicles and pedestrians. The aerobatic pilot says staying calm and making good decisions helped bring the flight to a safe ending.

recentItems.title: Driver on drugs blew red light before fatal work zone crash, prosecutors say
recentItems.description:
A 26-year-old man is accused of driving the wrong way, running a red light, and crashing into a road construction zone, killing one worker and seriously injuring two others. Prosecutors say surveillance video showed Thomas Lobianco stumbling before the crash and allege drugs were recovered from his vehicle and backpack. The defense argues toxicology results are not yet complete. Bail was set at $7.5 million cash or $15 million bond. Joel Sicon-Porix of Mastic was killed in the crash.

recentItems.title: Machetes, knives recovered after violent Port Chester garage fight
recentItems.description:
Multiple people were injured after two groups of men armed with machetes, knives and razor blades clashed inside the Metro-North Port Chester Station parking garage. Police say the violence may have stemmed from an earlier confrontation in downtown Port Chester that involved a shirt being burned and posted on social media. Four people were charged with criminal possession of a weapon, while investigators recovered six blades and a lighter believed to be connected to the earlier incident. The investigation remains ongoing, and no assault charges have been filed at this time.

recentItems.title: Newly released 9/11 air quality records reveal high levels of toxins
recentItems.description:
New York City is releasing more than 170,000 records related to air quality testing following the Sept. 11 attacks, including air sample data, correspondence and internal memos. Advocates and first responders say the release is long overdue and could provide new insight into environmental toxin concerns tied to 9/11-related illnesses. The documents will be made available through a public online portal as investigations continue.

recentItems.title: The Man in the Red Bandana: Welles Crowther awarded Presidential Medal of Freedom
recentItems.description:
Welles Crowther, known as the “Man in the Red Bandana,” was posthumously awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor. During a White House ceremony marking the anniversary of 9/11, his mother Alison Crowther accepted the award on behalf of her late son, who is believed to have saved as many as 18 lives while guiding people to safety from the South Tower of the World Trade Center. Twenty-five years later, his courage, compassion and service continue to inspire.

recentItems.title: “Run!”: FDNY firefighter recalls the moment the South Tower collapsed
recentItems.description:
Former FDNY firefighter Kevin Shea was off duty when he learned a plane had struck the World Trade Center. After the second plane hit, he responded with fellow firefighters and headed toward the South Tower. Shea recalls the chaos, the collapse and surviving after being partially buried by debris. He now reflects on the injuries he suffered and the lives lost that day.
